route: Strasbourg → Bourscheid Castle viewpoint → Liège-Guillemins → Emmen
intro:
After breakfast this morning, I left my hotel in Strasbourg at about eight o’clock. Something happened that hadn’t happened on any other day of this trip, even in the mountains: when I got to the car, the windows were iced over. I spent part of the morning defrosting them. It’s interesting that I’d been in colder places, yet today was the first time I encountered ice on the car.

I hadn’t seen much of Strasbourg itself, and with reports of a large protest planned in France, I was eager to get on the road.

As I drove along the motorway toward Luxembourg, the landscape became hillier. Small towns appeared through the morning haze as the sun rose, making for a picturesque scene. Traffic added about thirty minutes to the drive, but I wasn’t particularly bothered. It was a calm morning, and I found myself thinking about the days ahead.

Luxembourg would be country number 13 of the 16 planned for this adventure.

As I made my way through Luxembourg, the roads wound through smaller towns, forests, and hills. Some were narrow, but the countryside was beautiful. There was something about the landscape that reminded me of a place where people would go camping or simply spend time enjoying nature.

I made my way to Bourscheid Castle, arriving around 11:15. I had been looking forward to this stop, imagining something a little more dramatic, something that would make me stop and say, “Wow.” But as the castle came into view in the distance, I found myself feeling a little underwhelmed. It wasn’t that the castle wasn’t impressive in its own right; it just didn’t quite stir the excitement I had expected. Maybe I’ve been spoiled by all the incredible places I’ve seen on this journey. After a while, I suppose it takes a little more to surprise me, and I found myself wondering if my expectations had simply gotten too high.

The viewing area didn’t help matters. There were logs piled up near a bench in what should have been one of the best spots to take in the castle, partially blocking the view. It felt a little awkward, as though I had arrived at the perfect place to admire the castle but couldn’t quite get the view I was hoping for.

In the end, though, I realized that the real beauty of this stop wasn’t necessarily the castle itself. It was the winding drive through the countryside, the rolling hills, and the scenery along the way. Sometimes the journey to a place leaves a bigger impression than the destination, and this was definitely one of those moments.

Leaving Luxembourg and entering Belgium, Apple Maps once again decided to take me along smaller back roads, winding between towns before connecting me to the E25 toward Liège. Thankfully, that portion of the drive didn’t last long.

Once on the motorway, I was surrounded by rolling hills, trees changing colors, and stretches of green grass. It wasn’t dramatic scenery, just a pleasant drive through the countryside.

Arriving in Liège, I found a city that felt comfortable in size, with a modern character that wasn’t overwhelming.

One of my stops was the Liège-Guillemins railway station, an impressive piece of modern architecture. I spent some time taking photographs and appreciating its design.

For lunch, I stopped at Tripick, where I tried a Belgian specialty: two meatballs served with a sauce containing raisins. The raisins weren’t particularly noticeable in the flavor, but the dish was comforting and enjoyable.

And then came dessert. Belgian waffles with caramel. The caramel was absolutely delightful and a wonderful way to finish lunch.

I was also surprised to find that French was the language spoken in Liège. It was another reminder of how much the cultures and languages can change as I travel through Europe.

After lunch, I began the drive north toward Emmen in the Netherlands. There was quite a bit of traffic along the way, but what really captured my attention was the scenery.

The canals were breathtaking.

I’d seen scenes like these in photographs before, but seeing them in person was something entirely different. The waterways, surrounding landscape, and character of the towns made me realize how many hidden gems there must be throughout the Netherlands. It’s definitely somewhere I’d like to return and explore further.

By around 5:30 in the evening, the sun had already been down for approximately half an hour. The days are getting noticeably shorter, and the chilly weather has been a constant companion throughout much of this journey.

As I was looking for my hotel in Emmen, I was surprised to see the Netherlands branch office along the way! I hadn’t realized it was so close. As it turns out, my hotel is just a few blocks away - literally a nine-minute walk or a two-minute drive. 🙂

Tomorrow morning, I’ll be visiting the branch at 10:00, something I’m really looking forward to. Afterward, I’ll begin the final leg of this adventure, heading back into Germany for the next few days.

It’s hard to believe that 18 days have already passed. It certainly doesn’t feel like it. I’ve traveled through so many different places and experienced so much, yet somehow it feels like this adventure only began a short time ago.

There are still a few days left in this adventure, and I’m looking forward to making the most of every one of them. It’s hard to believe how quickly the time has passed.

And with today’s travels, I’ve now visited 15 countries, with just one more to go. And no, it’s not Germany! Perhaps I’ve saved the best for last. I guess we’ll have to wait and see. 🙂

stops.name: Emmen
stops.description: A city in the Dutch province of Drenthe, known for its green spaces and nearby prehistoric hunebed monuments.
